messages:
alex: Customer noticed their monthly credits dropped to 0 about an hour before their local midnight refill. Tenant is on CET (Europe/Berlin). They reported 429s across multiple services and UI showed 0/1000 credits at 23:10 local.

maria: Oof. Do we have tenant id + plan? Can you paste the exact 429 response headers if available? :eyes: Was this a streaming session or a burst of many short requests?

alex: Tenant ID t-9823, plan "startup-monthly-1k". They say they were running an internal load test around 22:55 CET (lots of concurrent 3-5s streaming sessions). Attached snippet from their logs: 

alex: ```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-medium","input":"test"}'

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 90
X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-Quota-Reset: 2405130000
Content-Type: application/json

{ "error": "quota_exhausted", "message": "monthly credits exhausted" }
```

maria: Thanks. X-Redwood-Quota-Reset header is helpful — looks like backend scheduled the reset at 2405130000 (00:00 UTC) in this case, which is 01:00 CET. But the UI is supposed to show tenant-local midnight. Could be a TZ conversion mismatch or cache TTL.

sre-oncall: Quick notes from infra: monthly refill job runs at 00:00 UTC. For tenants with local-midnight semantics we translate and schedule a tenant-specific refill at the corresponding UTC time. There was an ongoing deployment to the billing worker last night that added a transient race where per-connection burst tokens could be double-counted when streams reconnect rapidly. We're investigating if that produced inflated consumption.

alex: Customer insists they should have refilled at 00:00 CET (23:00 UTC). They expected refill earlier because their org billing timezone is set to Europe/Berlin. They saw UI go to 0 at 23:10 CET and refill to 1000 at 00:15 CET.

maria: Two things to confirm for repro: 1) whether billing timezone for t-9823 was incorrectly set to UTC instead of Europe/Berlin, and 2) whether streaming reconnection increments tokens twice. Can you ask customer to share a short HAR or sample stream logs around the time (22:50-00:20 CET)?

alex: Asked customer for HAR. They provided logs showing many WS reconnects at 23:05-23:08 CET. Example from their stream supervisor: 

alex: ```
[23:05:02 CET] stream_id=aa12 reconnect attempt=1 tokens_sent=120
[23:05:05 CET] stream_id=aa12 reconnect attempt=2 tokens_sent=130
[23:05:09 CET] stream_id=aa12 reconnect attempt=3 tokens_sent=125
```

sre-oncall: That pattern could cause double accounting if the server finalizes token counts on both the old and new connection before garbage collection. We'll instrument the stream accounting to detect duplicate finalize events. For mitigation, ask customer to: 1) pause load test until we confirm, 2) we can manually top-up 500 credits as goodwill while we investigate.

maria: I'll provision a one-time 500 credit top-up and escalate billing config check. alex, can you confirm whether tenant's billing timezone appears as CET in the admin console and send a screenshot?

alex: Sent screenshot — tenant timezone is set to Europe/Berlin in the console. Screenshot timestamped 2026-03-17 09:12 UTC.

billing-bot: Automated note: created support ticket #SUP-2026-452 for manual top-up and billing-worker investigation. Assigned to eng-infra (priority P2).

sre-oncall: Next steps for infra: 1) run a targeted query for finalize events for t-9823 between 22:50-23:20 CET to detect duplicates, 2) add temporary guard in stream accounting to ignore duplicate finalize within 10s per stream_id, 3) verify refill scheduler maps tenant-local midnight correctly (edgecases: DST) and add unit tests.

maria: Customer accepted the temporary top-up. They want ETA on permanent fix and confirmation of why UI showed 0 earlier than expected.

sre-oncall: ETA: hotfix for duplicate finalize guard today (3–4 hours); refill scheduler tests and DST edgecase fix planned for next week. UI showing 0 early is likely cache TTL + frontend conversion: UI queries cached quota state from cache layer that can be stale for up to 5–10 minutes after backend adjustments. We'll add an explicit cache purge after refill job as part of the follow-up.

alex: I'll reply to customer with: 1) we applied 500 credits now, 2) temporary mitigation steps, 3) root causes under investigation (stream reconnection double-counting + cache/display mismatch), 4) ETA for hotfix and follow-up.

maria: Sounds good. Please include repro logs and ticket id SUP-2026-452. :thumbsup:

alex: Done. Customer replied: "Thanks — please keep us posted, the load test is paused."

maria: Closing internal thread once infra confirms hotfix deployed. Leave notes in SUP-2026-452.

sre-oncall: Will update thread when hotfix and accounting query results are in.

alex: Marking this resolved from support side for now. Will reopen if customer sees repeat behavior.
